source_ref: van Eersel JHW, Wickham MI, Smid GE, Boelen PA (2024) 'Pre-job loss grief reactions and work attachment among sick-listed employees: Introduction of the imminent Job Loss Scale', BMC Psychology 12:118, doi:10.1186/s40359-024-01626-8 (PMC10909267, CC BY 4.0) -- Table 2 (English items 1-9 with CFA loadings), Table 1 (IJLS sum M=28.7 SD=7.7), Supplementary Material 1 = Appendix (the original Dutch version, 'Vragenlijst Dreigend Verlies van Werk', items 1-9), Supplementary Material 2 (expert-panel ratings of the selected and unselected items). Data deposit: DataverseNL doi:10.34894/FDDFTJ (CC0-1.0), files 'IJLS [dataset].sav' (file 378450; SPSS variable labels and value labels for IJLS_1..IJLS_9 and IJLS_1_T2..IJLS_9_T2), 'IJLS_readme.txt' (file 378452; codebook listing each variable with its English item text and its 1-5 anchor coding) and 'IJLS [dataset].dat' (file 378451; the tab-delimited file the IRW script reads). Processing script data/IJLS_Eersel_2024.R. All cached under .cache/IJLS_Eersel_2024_IJLSreaction/.
note: CODE DERIVATION (core model 3, first pattern -- exempt from Step 5b): the IRW item codes IJLS_1..IJLS_9 ARE the column names of the deposit's own .dat/.sav files. data/IJLS_Eersel_2024.R does select(id, contains('IJLS')) then pivot_longer(IJLS_1:IJLS_9_T2, names_to='item'), i.e. the code is the source column name taken by name, with no positional or renaming step; the only edit is substr(1,6) applied to the retest columns, which strips the '_T2' suffix and sets wave=1. That collapse is label-safe: the .sav gives IJLS_i and IJLS_i_T2 identical variable labels for all nine i. MAPPING BASIS = data_labels: the .sav's own variable labels tie each code to its item text ('IJLS_1' -> '1. I longed strongly for how my life was before the impending loss of my job.', ... 'IJLS_9' -> '9. I felt lonely because of my job loss'), 9/9, and IJLS_readme.txt repeats the same nine code->text lines with the anchor coding appended. Value labels tie the resp axis: 1=Never 2=Rarely 3=Sometimes 4=Often 5=Always on every IJLS_i (the _T2 twins carry the same five labels with 'Rarely' misspelled 'Rarily' -- a source typo in columns this table does not ship, noted only so a later reader is not surprised by it). CORROBORATION, computed from the deposit's .dat with no live export: summing IJLS_1..IJLS_9 raw over the 200 T1 respondents gives M=28.64, SD=7.67 against the paper's printed 28.7 / 7.7, so the block is the IJLS and it is stored RAW and ascending (1=never), not reverse-scored; and per-item live n=367 for all nine items (irw_table_sets) equals the deposit's 200 T1 + 167 T2 rows exactly, confirming the wave collapse. TEXT: item_text is the Dutch Appendix wording transcribed verbatim, with only the leading '1. '..'9. ' numbering removed. item_text_translated is the paper's Table 2 English, verbatim, with one repair: the Europe PMC XML of Table 2 renders item 1 as 'before theimpending loss', a lost space from the typeset PDF, restored to 'before the impending loss'. Table 2 was preferred over the .sav/readme English because the Appendix names it as the English version of the scale and because its item 9 ('because of my impending job loss') matches the Dutch original, where the .sav/readme label drops 'impending'; that variant is recorded in notes. Leading item numbers and the .sav's stray trailing full stop on item 1 were stripped. OPTION AXIS: option_text ships the .sav value labels, which are ENGLISH; no Dutch anchors appear in the deposit, in either supplement or in the paper, so option_text_translated is left empty and the base field is the documented English fallback for that field only. This project translated nothing -- translation_source=study_supplied throughout. instructions and section_prompt are blank: no verbatim instruction text is published (the paper says only that participants rated the preceding four weeks on a 1-5 scale), and there is no testlet structure, so section_id is the single trivial IJLS_Eersel_2024_IJLSreaction_1. correct_response is blank: a frequency scale has no key. STEP 3B (instrument-mismatch check, and this study has eight IRW tables from one .dat file): the live item set is exactly IJLS_1..IJLS_9 on resp 1-5, the nine columns named IJLS_* in the source header, and the sum reproduces the paper's IJLS statistic -- so this table is the IJLS itself, not one of the sibling instruments in the same file (HADS A1-A7/D1-D7, LOT-R Lot_r_1..6, IUS_1..12, ICECAP1r..5r, BC_* denial/acceptance, WorkCen/UWES/commit). RIGHTS: no restriction found and none quotable. The IJLS is introduced by this CC BY 4.0 paper, which prints all nine items itself and deposits the Dutch original as a supplement under the same licence; the data deposit is CC0-1.0. Silence is permission (2026-09-04). RETRY TEST: NO -- a determinate verdict was reached and the table shipped.

The response anchors are the exception: no Dutch anchors are published in the deposit or the paper, so option_text shows the English labels from the study's SPSS value labels (1 = Never to 5 = Always) rather than what respondents read

source_ref: https://www.imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/1987/1987_eng.pdf (official English problem paper, 28th IMO, Havana, Cuba); scores: https://www.imo-official.org/results/individual/year/1987/; response data: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/luckyt/imo-scores (imo_results.csv), processed by data/imos_2018.r
note: Item text transcribed from the official IMO 1987 English problem paper, whose printed numbering 1-6 matches the live item codes problem1-problem6 (the processing script pivots the source CSV's own problem1..problem6 columns, so the code is the source column name, not a positional assignment). Typeset mathematics rendered in plain-text/LaTeX-style notation (p_n(k), x_1^2, sqrt(n), <=, >=) since the source is LaTeX-typeset; wording otherwise verbatim including the official paper's own typo in problem 3, which prints '|a_1 x_1 + a_1 x_2 + ... + a_n x_n|' where the second coefficient should be a_2. instructions left blank: the official paper carries no participant instructions, only the day/date headers, which are recorded as section_prompt for the Day I (problems 1-3) and Day II (problems 4-6) papers. option_text left blank for every row: resp is the 0-7 mark awarded by the jury for a written proof, not a selected response option, so no option wording exists and none was invented. Option rows are emitted for all 8 marks 0-7 for every problem because that is the official mark range for each problem; no contestant scored 4 on problem 3, so that one level is unused in the live data. Instrument identity confirmed against the data: 237 contestants and 6 problems match the 28th IMO (Havana, 10-11 July 1987) exactly, and the live per-item mark distributions reproduce imo-official.org's own 1987 P1-P6 columns cell for cell (48/48).
public_note: Item text is the official English version of the IMO 1987 paper; the competition is administered in each contestant's own language, so most of the 237 contestants read a translation of this wording rather than the English printed here.

source_ref: https://www.imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/1988/1988_eng.pdf (official IMO archive, 29th IMO, Canberra 1988, problems numbered 1-6); scores cross-checked against https://www.imo-official.org/results/individual/year/1988/
note: Item text transcribed verbatim from the official IMO 1988 English problem PDF; the archive numbers the problems 1-6 and the IRW codes are problem1..problem6, taken straight from the Problem1..Problem6 columns of imo_results.csv (data/imos_2018.r renames nothing but lowercases). Deviations disclosed: the PDF's typeset mathematics is rendered as plain text (BC^2, A_1, sum_{k=1}^{70} k/(x - k), Unicode kept for the source's own intersection/inequality signs); Problem 4's missing article is the source's own -- the PDF reads 'Show that set of real numbers x', transcribed as printed. instructions left blank: the official PDF publishes no rubric or instructions text, only the two day headers, which are recorded as section_prompt 'Day I' (problems 1-3) and 'Day II' (problems 4-6). option_text is blank for every row by design: resp 0-7 is the IMO's marks-out-of-7 with no verbal anchors, and unlabelled points are not padded with their own number. No rights restriction found on imo-official.org for the problem archive; nothing quotable, so silence-is-permission applies. Mapping verified: all 6 items x 8 score levels reproduce the official per-problem score distributions exactly (see verify_imos_1988.R).
public_note: The IMO administers each year's paper in every contestant's own language (268 contestants from 49 countries in 1988); the item text shipped here is the organisers' official English version, not a single administered wording.
